item: A forward step of the wall clock is recorded against the boot-time clock, marks the gap it made, and counts in a never-capped counter that is null until measured
summary: Finding 6 of the vitals read: a forward wall-clock correction left a gap in the five-minute rows that read as down time. tick() now takes (wall advance) - (boot-time advance) between consecutive ticks from CLOCK_BOOTTIME (session_history.boottime(); no second reader): 0 for a stalled thread, a frozen process or a suspend the kernel measured, a number only where the wall clock was moved. A step is recorded in the shared clock_steps list (forward_s; newest 20) and counted in clock_stepped_forward (never capped) from 600 s (the span _gaps lists a gap from) or, below that, from 1 s where it is what opened a listed gap; one _opens_gap rule feeds _gaps and tick because ticks fall anywhere in their bucket (the first read's probes, a step of 595.5 s at offset 299.9, 596 s at 299.5, 599 s at 297, 585 s on a tick 20 s late, each left a 600 s unmarked gap under the 'smallest step is 600 s' derivation, which holds only on a 5 s grid aligned to the buckets). A step under 600 s inside a gap the process's absence opened anyway is deliberately not recorded and the method lists it. The counter is null (not 0) until a tick has had a boot-time clock to compare with, the boot-time clock is read on both sides of the wall read and the pair is used only within 0.1 s, tick(now=, mono=) without boot= means no boot clock, and both counters clamp at 0 on restore. Linux only; not measured across a restart or on a session's first tick; no cause is claimed. A forward record is 78 bytes; the method text is 3.7 KB and the member keeps about 13 KB under its 260,000-byte budget. One independent read (0 block, 2 should-fix, 6 low) and one delta read of its fold (0 block, 1 should-fix, 3 low), both folded; 36 mutants killed; 768 tests in the ten affected files.
